concerns.text: The plan assumes the TUH EEG Corpus contains 'Cognitive Scores' (MMSE/MoCA) for a subset of participants sufficient for power analysis (FR-004). The TUH Abnormal/Normal corpora primarily contain clinical notes and diagnosis codes, not structured, standardized cognitive assessment scores (MMSE/MoCA) in the metadata. Relying on this dataset for the primary outcome (cognitive decline correlation) is likely infeasible as the required data field is likely absent or unstructured in the source, making the planned statistical analysis impossible without a different dataset or a different outcome variable.

The plan targets a sample size sufficient for power >= 0.80 at r=0.3 for the correlation between network metrics and cognitive scores. Given the likely absence of structured cognitive scores in the TUH dataset (see above), the effective N for this specific analysis will be near zero. The plan fails to identify a fallback dataset (e.g., ADNI, HCP-Aging) that actually contains both resting-state EEG and standardized cognitive scores, rendering the statistical power goal unachievable with the cited resource.
